_meta.title: WPBRC Current Issues
_meta.disclaimer: Working drafts. Positions are pending Board confirmation; key dates, studies, and meetings should be verified against official City of West Palm Beach agendas before publication.

issues.title: Downtown Master Plan
issues.summary: Long-range decisions that will shape downtown and the waterfront for decades — including building heights, density, and the public review process.
issues.why: The Downtown Master Plan (DMP) sets the rules for height, density, and land use across the city core. Proposed changes could add over 1,200 high-rise units along the waterfront corridor, with towers ranging from roughly 18 to 31 stories. Residents are asking for adequate time to review mobility and infrastructure impacts before the plan is finalized.
keyDates: Apr 25, 2024 — Comprehensive Plan / DMP element adopted (Ord. 5071-23)
2025–2026 — DMP update process underway at the Planning Division
Verify upcoming Downtown Action Committee (DAC) and Commission dates against the City calendar

issues.title: Traffic & Mobility
issues.summary: How new growth affects congestion, parking, transit, and pedestrian and cyclist safety across the city.
issues.why: Each major project adds trips to roads that were not designed for this pace of growth. Residents want long-term planning aligned with the County Transportation Master Plan and regional mobility studies, not project-by-project review.
keyDates: Verify against the County Transportation Planning Agency (TPA) meeting calendar
meetings: Palm Beach TPA board meetings — add dates to the Calendar
issues.position: Draft — pending Board confirmation: Align long-term city planning with the County Transportation Master Plan and regional mobility studies; fund independent traffic and mobility analysis.
plan: Commission or compile independent traffic and mobility analysis
Map cumulative trip impacts from the development pipeline
Advocate for a coordinated, citywide mobility approach

issues.title: Infrastructure Capacity
issues.summary: Whether water, sewer, drainage, and stormwater systems can support the scale of approved and proposed growth.
issues.why: Much of the city's infrastructure is aging. Rapid high-density growth raises questions about capacity for water, sewer, drainage, and resilience that residents want answered before, not after, approvals.
keyDates: Tie to City budget and Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) cycles — verify dates
meetings: City Commission budget / CIP workshops — add to Calendar
issues.position: Draft — pending Board confirmation: Infrastructure capacity and resilience should be evaluated and disclosed before major approvals.
plan: Request capacity and CIP documentation through public records
Summarize findings in plain language for residents
Track infrastructure commitments tied to each major project

issues.title: Public Safety
issues.summary: Police, fire-rescue, and neighborhood safety keeping pace with population growth.
issues.why: A growing residential downtown and denser neighborhoods change demands on police and fire-rescue. Residents want service levels and response times to keep pace with growth.
keyDates: Tie to City budget cycle — verify dates
meetings: Neighborhood public-safety briefings — add to Calendar
issues.position: Draft — pending Board confirmation: Public-safety staffing and response capacity should scale with new development.
plan: Track public-safety staffing and budget against growth

issues.title: Waterfront Planning
issues.summary: Protecting public access, green space, views, and the Intracoastal ecosystem along the waterfront.
issues.why: The waterfront is a shared public asset. Proposed towers along the corridor raise concerns about shadows on historic neighborhoods, public access, and the health of the Intracoastal ecosystem, seagrass, and manatees.
keyDates: Verify against DAC and Commission waterfront agenda items
meetings: Waterfront-related Commission and DAC hearings — add to Calendar
issues.position: Draft — pending Board confirmation: Protect public waterfront access, green space, and environmental resilience for the long term.
plan: Track waterfront projects on the Development Tracker

Support resident participation in waterfront decisions

issues.title: Development Pipeline
issues.summary: The full slate of major projects proposed, approved, and under construction across the city.
issues.why: Dozens of major projects are moving through the pipeline from Northwood to SoSo. Looking at them together — not one at a time — is the only way to understand the cumulative impact on traffic, infrastructure, and neighborhood character.
keyDates: Updated continuously — see the Development Tracker

issues.position: Draft — pending Board confirmation: Evaluate growth cumulatively and transparently so it strengthens neighborhoods.
plan: Publish a plain-language summary of cumulative impacts
